extraction.name: POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation)
extraction.description: A polling-based evaluation method for object hallucination in large vision-language models. It converts hallucination evaluation into a binary yes/no probing task and is designed to be more stable and flexible than instruction-based evaluation.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The evaluation questions were built on POPE using the validation set of MSCOCO; the authors randomly selected 500 images with more than one object and constructed questions under Random, Popular, and Adversarial settings. They also used SEEM to annotate images from MSCOCO to build a segmentation-based version of POPE.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The validation set of MSCOCO images, specifically 500 randomly selected images with more than one object; for the SEEM-based variant, images from MSCOCO were automatically annotated with segmentation results.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: CHAIR metric is used to evaluate hallucination; the paper reports results on several models and discusses instability of CHAIR across instructions, but no human annotation agreement or validation analysis is described.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that object hallucination can occur in LVLM-generated captions and that hallucinations may be considered at different semantic levels, but this section does not discuss dataset-specific biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The described issue is that LVLMs can generate hallucinated objects in captions, which hinders safe real-world deployment. The section also states that fine-grained hallucinations such as number, attributes, and positions are left for future work.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper indicates a negative social/safety implication: hallucinations can hinder safe real-world deployment of LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The section describes LVLM training stages and mentions use on multimodal tasks such as visual question answering, but it does not specify dataset use cases or usage guidelines for this dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper analyzes visual instruction data and uses object sampling strategies for evaluation, including selecting top frequent objects and top co-occurring objects with a target object (e.g., "dining table").
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The evaluation uses MSCOCO images and captions, with captions generated from two prompts and then scored using CHAIR; the paper does not describe dataset cleaning or normalization steps.

name.evidence: we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination.

description.evidence: The basic idea is to convert the evaluation of hallucination into a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with simple Yes-or-No short questions about the probing objects ... We show that such a method is more stable and flexible.
